world.title: IEA says Hormuz disruption threatens global energy security, speeds shift
world.summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Nov. 19 that the Middle East conflict and Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz pose the greatest threat to energy security in the agency’s history, disrupting oil exports and leaving consumers facing higher prices and, in some places, supply shortfalls. Before the crisis
world.content: The International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Nov. 19 that the Middle East conflict and Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz pose the greatest threat to energy security in the agency’s history, disrupting oil exports and leaving consumers facing higher prices and, in some places, supply shortfalls. Before the crisis, about one-fifth of global oil shipments passed through the strait; U.S. attempts to escort vessels have not restored normal flows. The agency’s annual World Energy Outlook says prolonged disruption could drive lasting changes in energy policy. In its middle scenario, oil demand peaks around 2030 and gas demand grows until about 2035; a new response scenario models greater electrification and lower fossil-fuel use if the crisis persists. Executive Director Fatih Birol said the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper its effects will be.
world.image_alt: IEA says Hormuz disruption threatens global energy security, speeds shift

world.title: US charges Russian man accused of spying on employees of Ukraine-linked Palantir
world.summary: U.S. prosecutors charged Russian national Igor D’iu with conspiring to act as a foreign agent, acting as an unregistered agent, interstate stalking and fraud. They allege he surveilled employees of Palantir, a technology and defense company that has supported Ukraine. The Justice Department says D’iu entered the United
world.content: U.S. prosecutors charged Russian national Igor D’iu with conspiring to act as a foreign agent, acting as an unregistered agent, interstate stalking and fraud. They allege he surveilled employees of Palantir, a technology and defense company that has supported Ukraine. The Justice Department says D’iu entered the United States through Mexico after traveling from Turkey, then followed workers, collected personal information and photographed laptop screens at a coffee shop near Palantir’s Palo Alto offices. The indictment did not name the company; Reuters and the BBC identified it as Palantir, citing sources familiar with the case. Prosecutors allege that D’iu received money, equipment and instructions from Russia-based contacts via Telegram, and that his handlers sought information because Palantir’s technology assisted Ukraine in its war with Russia. The FBI says agents found cash, Russian passports, forged identification and information about employees at his East Palo Alto home. D’iu remains in federal custody and is scheduled to appear in court on Nov. 24. He could face up to 21 years in prison if convicted on all counts.
world.image_alt: US charges Russian man accused of spying on employees of Ukraine-linked Palantir

world.title: Bangladesh faces shutdown as arsonists target Yunus’s ancestral home
world.summary: Unidentified attackers late Wednesday set fire to an unused ground-floor room in the Chattogram home of Muhammad Yunus, who led Bangladesh’s interim government after Sheikh Hasina’s ouster. Police extinguished the blaze and strengthened security around the house. They said Yunus’s relatives living upstairs were safe. I
world.content: Unidentified attackers late Wednesday set fire to an unused ground-floor room in the Chattogram home of Muhammad Yunus, who led Bangladesh’s interim government after Sheikh Hasina’s ouster. Police extinguished the blaze and strengthened security around the house. They said Yunus’s relatives living upstairs were safe. Investigators have not identified those responsible. Hasina’s banned Awami League called a nationwide shutdown for Thursday, the anniversary of the tribunal verdict that sentenced her to death in absentia over the 2024 crackdown on student protests. The unrest has included crude-bomb blasts, arson and clashes across 28 districts. Police said two local Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leaders were killed in Narail, while blasts in Dhaka injured at least four people. Authorities arrested 565 people in Dhaka in a 24-hour operation and deployed border guards in sensitive areas. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said perpetrators would be identified and prosecuted. The Awami League has also protested the government’s rejection of Hasina’s request for travel documents. She has said she plans to return from India in December.
world.image_alt: Bangladesh faces shutdown as arsonists target Yunus’s ancestral home

world.title: European allies meet in Berlin as Trump and Putin discuss Ukraine
world.summary: European leaders and Ukrainian officials are meeting U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Berlin on Thursday as European governments seek a role in U.S.-led efforts to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. The Coalition of the Willing gathering includes the leaders of Germany, France, Britain, Poland and Italy, as wel
world.content: European leaders and Ukrainian officials are meeting U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Berlin on Thursday as European governments seek a role in U.S.-led efforts to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. The Coalition of the Willing gathering includes the leaders of Germany, France, Britain, Poland and Italy, as well as NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte. German officials said the discussions would cover legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine after a ceasefire, economic recovery and preparations for another round of multilateral negotiations. The meeting coincides with President Donald Trump’s talks in Shenzhen with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. European officials are concerned that decisions affecting Ukraine and Europe could be made without them. Last week’s U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi—the first involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. officials in nine months—produced no breakthrough on ending the war, though the sides agreed to a prisoner exchange. Russia is seeking Ukraine’s Donbas region, while Kyiv opposes giving up territory. European allies say the Berlin meeting will let them respond quickly to developments in China. EU leaders are due to discuss a proposed Ukraine loan in Brussels next week.
world.image_alt: European allies meet in Berlin as Trump and Putin discuss Ukraine

world.title: Iran widens Gulf attacks as energy agency warns of historic threat
world.summary: Iran said it targeted a U.S. air base in Kuwait on Wednesday, while Bahrain said it intercepted several attacks and issued shelter alerts. Kuwait said its air defenses intercepted drones. The attacks followed a U.S. strike on a missile-launch site on Iran’s Qeshm Island and Iranian attacks on a U.S. radar installation
world.content: Iran said it targeted a U.S. air base in Kuwait on Wednesday, while Bahrain said it intercepted several attacks and issued shelter alerts. Kuwait said its air defenses intercepted drones. The attacks followed a U.S. strike on a missile-launch site on Iran’s Qeshm Island and Iranian attacks on a U.S. radar installation in Bahrain. The war began with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. The International Energy Agency (IEA) said the conflict and disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz now pose the largest threat to energy security in its history. The strait carried about one-fifth of global oil shipments before the war, and the agency warned that consumers increasingly face higher prices and supply shortfalls as other buffers run down. Qatar said its officials met Iranian negotiators on Tuesday to narrow differences, while Iran’s foreign minister also met his Omani counterpart. The U.S. has maintained a naval blockade of Iranian ports.
world.image_alt: Iran widens Gulf attacks as energy agency warns of historic threat

world.title: UN court set to rule on Myanmar’s alleged Rohingya genocide
world.summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the United Nations’ top court, is scheduled to rule Thursday, Nov. 19, on The Gambia’s 2019 case accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. The case concerns the military’s 2017 crackdown in Rakhine State, which drove at least 730,000 Rohingya into Bangl
world.content: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the United Nations’ top court, is scheduled to rule Thursday, Nov. 19, on The Gambia’s 2019 case accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. The case concerns the military’s 2017 crackdown in Rakhine State, which drove at least 730,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh. Survivors have described killings, mass rape and burned villages. Myanmar denies genocide and says its forces were responding to attacks by armed groups. The court’s 15 judges must decide whether Myanmar, as a state, breached the 1948 Genocide Convention, including whether the alleged acts were carried out with intent to destroy the Rohingya, in whole or in part. The ICJ has never found a state to have committed genocide, and legal experts say the ruling could shape how the court handles other cases, including South Africa’s case against Israel. The court is due to begin reading the judgment in The Hague at 10 a.m. local time, a process expected to take up to 90 minutes. The Gambia has asked the court to order reparations and the safe return of refugees. The ruling will be final, but enforcement options are limited and could involve the U.N. Security Council.
world.image_alt: UN court set to rule on Myanmar’s alleged Rohingya genocide

world.title: Miami jury convicts Haitian-American pastor in Moïse assassination plot
world.summary: A federal jury in Miami convicted Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a Haitian-American pastor, on all eight charges tied to the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse, including conspiring to kill or kidnap someone outside the United States. Sanon faces up to life in prison and is scheduled to be sentenced on Fe
world.content: A federal jury in Miami convicted Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a Haitian-American pastor, on all eight charges tied to the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse, including conspiring to kill or kidnap someone outside the United States. Sanon faces up to life in prison and is scheduled to be sentenced on February 10, 2027. Prosecutors said South Florida was a planning and financing hub for a scheme to remove Moïse and install a president chosen by the conspirators. They described Sanon as the initial choice and said he helped raise money and arrange travel and lodging. Sanon acknowledged contact with people seeking to replace Moïse but testified that the group had shifted to another candidate before the killing. He denied knowing about a murder plan. The verdict followed a nearly eight-week trial. Sanon’s lawyer, Zeljka Bozanic, said the defense would appeal. Prosecutors have charged more than 40 people in the case, and a dozen have been convicted, including five serving life terms. Other defendants remain in the U.S. case, and Haiti is scheduled to elect a new president in 2027.
world.image_alt: Miami jury convicts Haitian-American pastor in Moïse assassination plot

world.title: Ukraine strikes Crimean bridge again, halting traffic before summit
world.summary: Russian-installed Crimean officials said a new attack halted traffic on the Kerch Bridge overnight into Thursday, the third reported strike on the crossing this week. Russia’s Transport Ministry said rail services were suspended and no one was hurt; officials were assessing the damage. The latest strike came two days a
world.content: Russian-installed Crimean officials said a new attack halted traffic on the Kerch Bridge overnight into Thursday, the third reported strike on the crossing this week. Russia’s Transport Ministry said rail services were suspended and no one was hurt; officials were assessing the damage. The latest strike came two days after Ukrainian drone and missile attacks brought down a major road span, destroying a 227-metre section. Rail traffic had resumed on one track before the latest suspension. The 19-kilometre bridge carries road and rail traffic between Russia and Crimea, which Moscow annexed in 2014, and has served as a supply route for Russian forces. The road damage has also disrupted shipping through the Kerch Strait, according to Deutsche Welle. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the earlier operation took weeks and unfolded in seven stages. Kyiv has described strikes on Russian infrastructure as retaliation for attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure. Officials were still assessing the bridge’s condition after the latest attack, and Ukrainian authorities had not commented on that strike by Thursday morning. The attack occurred hours before Russian President Vladimir Putin, U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were due to meet in Shenzhen.
world.image_alt: Ukraine strikes Crimean bridge again, halting traffic before summit

business.title: Australia loses 43,500 jobs as unemployment hits five-year high
business.summary: Australia’s unemployment rate rose to 4.9% in October, its highest since 2021, as employment fell by 43,500 in a second consecutive monthly decline, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported Thursday. The figures fell well short of forecasts for job growth and prompted financial markets to price out further Reserve
business.content: Australia’s unemployment rate rose to 4.9% in October, its highest since 2021, as employment fell by 43,500 in a second consecutive monthly decline, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported Thursday. The figures fell well short of forecasts for job growth and prompted financial markets to price out further Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) rate increases. Traders assigned a 68% chance of a rate cut in June 2027 and about 90% in August. Employment is weakening while inflation remains high, after five RBA rate increases this year lifted the cash rate to 4.85%, an 18-year high. Markets expect the RBA to hold rates at its December 8 meeting, while banks see a possible cut next August.
business.image_alt: Australia loses 43,500 jobs as unemployment hits five-year high

business.title: German watchdog probes Deutsche Bank after 15 million-file leak
business.summary: The data-protection commissioner in Germany’s Hesse state opened an investigation into Deutsche Bank on Nov. 18 to examine whether the lender had adequate safeguards for more than 15 million leaked internal records and promptly notified regulators and affected people. Reports based on the files examine past dealings wi
business.content: The data-protection commissioner in Germany’s Hesse state opened an investigation into Deutsche Bank on Nov. 18 to examine whether the lender had adequate safeguards for more than 15 million leaked internal records and promptly notified regulators and affected people. Reports based on the files examine past dealings with clients including Russian oligarchs, Jeffrey Epstein and President Donald Trump, and allege that the bank overlooked internal warnings and promoted tax-planning structures for wealthy clients. The inquiry concerns the handling of the data, not whether the business practices described in the records broke the law. Deutsche Bank said its security testing found no indication that anyone had accessed account information, login credentials or payment data, and that the matters described in the reports dated back years. Its shares fell as much as 6% on Tuesday, Nov. 17; the bank said it did not expect a meaningful financial impact from the disclosures. The regulator has requested further information and documents from the bank.
business.image_alt: German watchdog probes Deutsche Bank after 15 million-file leak

business.title: Medicare Part B premiums rise $6.50 a month for 2027
business.summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the federal agency that administers Medicare, said the standard monthly Medicare Part B premium will rise $6.50 to $209.40 in 2027, while the annual deductible will increase $9 to $292. CMS attributed the increases mainly to projected growth in health care spending. T
business.content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the federal agency that administers Medicare, said the standard monthly Medicare Part B premium will rise $6.50 to $209.40 in 2027, while the annual deductible will increase $9 to $292. CMS attributed the increases mainly to projected growth in health care spending. The premium change will take effect with January 2027 payments. For people whose Part B premiums are deducted from Social Security checks, the 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment is expected to increase the average retired worker’s benefit by about $75 a month; after accounting for the higher premium, the increase will be about $68.50. Higher-income enrollees and people with hospital or prescription drug coverage face additional cost changes, including higher Part A hospital cost sharing and a higher standard Part D deductible.
business.image_alt: Medicare Part B premiums rise $6.50 a month for 2027

business.title: Carney presses U.S. for trade deal while expanding China ties
business.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a trade agreement with the United States remains possible but is not close to completion. He met President Donald Trump for just under 20 minutes on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. Carney said Canada would not accept a deal that did not
business.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a trade agreement with the United States remains possible but is not close to completion. He met President Donald Trump for just under 20 minutes on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. Carney said Canada would not accept a deal that did not serve its interests and described negotiations with Washington as more complex than those with Beijing. The meeting followed a new Canada-China agreement under which Beijing will lower tariffs on about 400 million Canadian dollars ($280 million) worth of exports, including pork, fish and seafood; Canada will extend exemptions for some Chinese steel and aluminum products by two years. U.S.-Canada talks collapsed in August, after which Washington imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion in Canadian goods and Ottawa retaliated. Carney said negotiations with the United States remain a priority. The leaders agreed to continue working toward a deal and stay in contact.
business.image_alt: Carney presses U.S. for trade deal while expanding China ties

business.title: Fed officials signal more rate hikes as inflation concerns spread
business.summary: Minutes released Nov. 18 from the Federal Reserve’s Oct. 27-28 meeting show that almost all participants judged further interest-rate increases likely needed to return inflation to the central bank’s 2% target. The Fed nevertheless held its benchmark rate at 3.75%-4% in October in a 10-2 vote; Governor Lisa Cook and Cl
business.content: Minutes released Nov. 18 from the Federal Reserve’s Oct. 27-28 meeting show that almost all participants judged further interest-rate increases likely needed to return inflation to the central bank’s 2% target. The Fed nevertheless held its benchmark rate at 3.75%-4% in October in a 10-2 vote; Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Officials described inflation pressures as broad-based and expressed concern that demand tied to artificial intelligence investment could add to price pressures. They also discussed financial-stability risks linked to AI-related borrowing and financing, while noting that they needed more information to assess investment demand, financing conditions and the effects of September’s rate increase. The Fed’s next policy meeting is Dec. 8-9. Governor Christopher Waller has urged consideration of a half-point increase, while New York Fed President John Williams has said the situation does not call for dramatic action. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly favors further increases at a measured pace.
business.image_alt: Fed officials signal more rate hikes as inflation concerns spread

business.title: Target lifts 2026 outlook after sales jump 7.1% before holidays
business.summary: Target raised its 2026 sales and earnings forecasts after third-quarter net sales rose 7.1% to $27.07 billion, its strongest quarterly sales growth in about five years. The Minneapolis retailer reported comparable sales growth of 5.6% for the three months ended Oct. 31, beating analyst expectations, and said sales so f
business.content: Target raised its 2026 sales and earnings forecasts after third-quarter net sales rose 7.1% to $27.07 billion, its strongest quarterly sales growth in about five years. The Minneapolis retailer reported comparable sales growth of 5.6% for the three months ended Oct. 31, beating analyst expectations, and said sales so far in November were in line with its full-year outlook. The company now expects full-year net sales to grow about 6%, up one percentage point from its August forecast, and earnings per share of $10.65 to $11.40. The earnings range includes a one-time benefit of $2.14 per share from tariff refunds. Target has cut prices, refreshed merchandise and expanded same-day delivery as part of its effort to restore growth. It plans to spend $5 billion to $6 billion on capital investments in 2027.
business.image_alt: Target lifts 2026 outlook after sales jump 7.1% before holidays

business.title: UK inflation reaches 3.6% as record diesel prices pressure households
business.summary: UK consumer-price inflation rose to 3.6% in October from 3.5% in September, its highest rate in a year, as fuel costs climbed. Motor-fuel prices rose 33.2% year over year; diesel averaged 199.5 pence a litre, a record in Office for National Statistics data dating back to 1996. The Bank of England’s inflation target is
business.content: UK consumer-price inflation rose to 3.6% in October from 3.5% in September, its highest rate in a year, as fuel costs climbed. Motor-fuel prices rose 33.2% year over year; diesel averaged 199.5 pence a litre, a record in Office for National Statistics data dating back to 1996. The Bank of England’s inflation target is 2%. Core inflation held at 2.8% and services inflation at 3.7%, while food and non-alcoholic drink inflation eased to 0.9%. The Bank raised its main rate to 4% earlier in November and has forecast inflation near 5% in 2027; analysts also expect household energy bills to rise sharply in January. The next inflation release is due Dec. 16, one day before the Bank’s next rate decision.
business.image_alt: UK inflation reaches 3.6% as record diesel prices pressure households

business.title: Palo Alto raises 2027 forecast and agrees to $4.5 billion AI deal
business.summary: Palo Alto Networks raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast and agreed to acquire AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock as the cybersecurity company reported quarterly revenue growth of 39%. The deal, subject to regulatory clearance, is expected to close in Palo Alto’s fiscal third quarter of 2027. The ac
business.content: Palo Alto Networks raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast and agreed to acquire AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock as the cybersecurity company reported quarterly revenue growth of 39%. The deal, subject to regulatory clearance, is expected to close in Palo Alto’s fiscal third quarter of 2027. The acquisition would add software and researchers for adapting and running open-weight AI models, which companies can customize using their own data. Palo Alto says it plans to offer the technology to customers deploying AI in public clouds or sovereign environments, expanding beyond security products. Chief Executive Nikesh Arora said AI is creating new security risks while driving demand for integrated platforms. The company now expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, up from its previous forecast of $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion. Palo Alto expects investment in Applied Compute’s integration to weigh on operating margins, with margins returning to their current range in fiscal 2029.
business.image_alt: Palo Alto raises 2027 forecast and agrees to $4.5 billion AI deal

science.title: Missouri researchers create audit to test AI
science.summary: University of Missouri researchers developed a framework to assess whether AI-generated themes capture the meaning of interview responses, not just recurring subjects. They tested it on 32 interviews with nursing faculty, practitioners and students discussing generative AI. For 11 of the 12 themes identified by human r
science.content: University of Missouri researchers developed a framework to assess whether AI-generated themes capture the meaning of interview responses, not just recurring subjects. They tested it on 32 interviews with nursing faculty, practitioners and students discussing generative AI. For 11 of the 12 themes identified by human researchers, the system generated a similar topic. Those matches did not guarantee accurate interpretation: the system sometimes merged distinct ideas or split a single theme into smaller topics, and researchers found limited evidence that it consistently uncovered new insights. The study, published in the International Journal of Qualitative Methods, calls for more testing across subject areas and research settings.
science.image_alt: Missouri researchers create audit to test AI

science.title: Experts say clustered tech outages expose risks in complex systems
science.summary: A series of technology failures affecting Microsoft services, U.S. air traffic, banks, Apple and the National Security Agency between Nov. 12 and 17 has prompted researchers to examine how routine changes can trigger failures in complex systems. Officials and companies have described separate technical problems. No con
science.content: A series of technology failures affecting Microsoft services, U.S. air traffic, banks, Apple and the National Security Agency between Nov. 12 and 17 has prompted researchers to examine how routine changes can trigger failures in complex systems. Officials and companies have described separate technical problems. No connection among the incidents or role for artificial intelligence has been established. The Federal Aviation Administration cited a telecommunications failure, while the NSA attributed its outage to scheduled maintenance. Experts say the timing alone does not establish a shared cause. Microsoft’s preliminary investigation found that a software bug introduced in July went unnoticed until a routine change shifted more traffic to affected servers. Researchers also note that companies cannot fully reproduce live systems in scaled-down test environments, limiting their ability to predict how updates will behave at full scale.
science.image_alt: Experts say clustered tech outages expose risks in complex systems

science.title: Mantle simulations offer an explanation for Earth
science.summary: Researchers at the University of Wollongong propose that slow movement in Earth’s mantle helped erase more than a billion years of geological history, then helped preserve the boundary that remains in rocks today. Their computer simulations indicate that deep currents lifted ancient continental regions, exposing rock t
science.content: Researchers at the University of Wollongong propose that slow movement in Earth’s mantle helped erase more than a billion years of geological history, then helped preserve the boundary that remains in rocks today. Their computer simulations indicate that deep currents lifted ancient continental regions, exposing rock to erosion, before the land sank and new sediment covered it. The proposed sequence could explain the Great Unconformity, a gap in rock layers found across several continents. The gap’s duration varies by location, from about 200 million years to more than a billion. The model’s pattern of uplift and sinking corresponds to evidence documented in North America, northern Europe and North China, but the researchers say mantle convection need not have been the only cause. The study was published in Nature, and the researchers say further work in other regions is needed.
science.image_alt: Mantle simulations offer an explanation for Earth

science.title: Experimental Alzheimer’s pill slows decline by 31% in patients taking no other Alzheimer’s drugs
science.summary: A phase 3 trial found that South Korean drugmaker AriBio’s experimental daily pill AR1001 slowed cognitive decline by 31% over 52 weeks among 604 people with early Alzheimer’s who were not taking other Alzheimer’s medicines. In the full trial of 1,535 people, which included participants taking other treatments, the dif
science.content: A phase 3 trial found that South Korean drugmaker AriBio’s experimental daily pill AR1001 slowed cognitive decline by 31% over 52 weeks among 604 people with early Alzheimer’s who were not taking other Alzheimer’s medicines. In the full trial of 1,535 people, which included participants taking other treatments, the difference from placebo was not statistically significant. AR1001 belongs to the same class as Viagra but is being developed specifically for Alzheimer’s. Experts warned against using Viagra for the disease and said the findings need further trials and regulatory review. The results were presented at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease conference in Boston, and AriBio plans to submit the full data to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
science.image_alt: Experimental Alzheimer’s pill slows decline by 31% in patients taking no other Alzheimer’s drugs

science.title: Vulcan failure linked to fuel supply after loss of Amazon satellites
science.summary: United Launch Alliance (ULA) said a preliminary review of its Nov. 15 Vulcan rocket failure points to inadequate fuel delivery to its two BE-4 first-stage engines, rather than an engine malfunction. The rocket failed to reach orbit, and all 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites aboard were lost in the first outright missi
science.content: United Launch Alliance (ULA) said a preliminary review of its Nov. 15 Vulcan rocket failure points to inadequate fuel delivery to its two BE-4 first-stage engines, rather than an engine malfunction. The rocket failed to reach orbit, and all 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites aboard were lost in the first outright mission failure in ULA’s history. ULA said the first stage underperformed shortly after liftoff, leaving the rocket too low and too slow at stage separation for the Centaur V upper stage to complete the mission. The company has not identified which fuel-system component failed or set a return-to-flight date. The Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing ULA’s investigation and will review its final report and corrective actions. Amazon’s next Leo launch is scheduled no earlier than Nov. 23 on an Ariane 6 rocket from French Guiana.
science.image_alt: Vulcan failure linked to fuel supply after loss of Amazon satellites

science.title: Three studies link gut microbes to diet, sterols and infection
science.summary: Three new studies examined how gut microbes interact with diet and the intestinal barrier. In a University of Copenhagen study of 75 vegans and 75 omnivores, vegans had lower average gut-bacterial diversity, although those with higher protein intake had diversity comparable to that of omnivores. The researchers stresse
science.content: Three new studies examined how gut microbes interact with diet and the intestinal barrier. In a University of Copenhagen study of 75 vegans and 75 omnivores, vegans had lower average gut-bacterial diversity, although those with higher protein intake had diversity comparable to that of omnivores. The researchers stressed that the observational study cannot establish cause and effect. A separate study found that gut bacteria convert dietary plant sterols into sulfated compounds detected in mouse tissues and human plasma. A third team engineered human intestinal tissues with immune cells and used them to study Salmonella infection. The sterol compounds’ effects remain unknown, and the engineered tissue study found that immune-cell signaling during bacterial invasion can damage the epithelial barrier.
science.image_alt: Three studies link gut microbes to diet, sterols and infection

science.title: White House withdraws Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead FDA before Senate vote
science.summary: The White House withdrew physician and domestic policy adviser Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead the Food and Drug Administration on Nov. 17, the night before a scheduled Senate committee vote. The administration said she lacked the votes. Sen. Bill Cassidy, chairman of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions
science.content: The White House withdrew physician and domestic policy adviser Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead the Food and Drug Administration on Nov. 17, the night before a scheduled Senate committee vote. The administration said she lacked the votes. Sen. Bill Cassidy, chairman of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, disputed that account, saying he believed she could win confirmation and that the dispute centered on anti-abortion senators’ demand for assurances on abortion policy. Overton faced senators’ questions about vaccines, food safety and abortion medication at a September hearing. Her withdrawal leaves the FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas, who has led the agency since former commissioner Martin Makary resigned in May. The White House has not announced a replacement, and Cassidy said confirmation of a permanent commissioner would fall to Senate Democrats when they take control in January.
science.image_alt: White House withdraws Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead FDA before Senate vote

science.title: Chad study finds eagles may prey on 26-kilogram baboons
science.summary: Researchers have found marks on bones and skulls suggesting Verreaux’s eagles preyed on adult male olive baboons in Chad’s Ennedi Plateau, including one estimated to have weighed 26.2 kilograms. The study, published Nov. 18 in the American Journal of Biological Anthropology, challenges a longstanding rule of thumb that
science.content: Researchers have found marks on bones and skulls suggesting Verreaux’s eagles preyed on adult male olive baboons in Chad’s Ennedi Plateau, including one estimated to have weighed 26.2 kilograms. The study, published Nov. 18 in the American Journal of Biological Anthropology, challenges a longstanding rule of thumb that primates above about 13 kilograms were effectively beyond avian predation. Previously, no primate heavier than that had been confirmed killed by a raptor. The team documented punctured eye sockets and talon-like scrapes on shoulder blades among the baboon remains. It did not witness a kill, so the researchers describe eagle predation as a likely explanation rather than a directly observed event. Some early hominins were in a similar weight range, but the findings do not establish that eagles hunted adult hominins or influenced their defensive behavior. The researchers plan further study of the isolated baboon population and its behavior.
science.image_alt: Chad study finds eagles may prey on 26-kilogram baboons

sports.title: World Cup winner Juan Mata retires at 38, keeps Melbourne Victory role
sports.summary: Former Spain, Chelsea and Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata announced his retirement from professional football on Nov. 18, ending a career that included winning the 2010 World Cup and major club trophies in England, Turkey and Japan. Mata, 38, earned 41 caps for Spain and scored in the 4-0 victory over Italy in t
sports.content: Former Spain, Chelsea and Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata announced his retirement from professional football on Nov. 18, ending a career that included winning the 2010 World Cup and major club trophies in England, Turkey and Japan. Mata, 38, earned 41 caps for Spain and scored in the 4-0 victory over Italy in the Euro 2012 final. His club career took him from Valencia to Chelsea and Manchester United, then to Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory. Mata holds a minority ownership stake in Melbourne Victory and chairs its football committee, a role he will continue after retiring. He also co-founded Common Goal, a football initiative supporting community projects. Mata said he would remain involved in the game, writing that he may stop playing professionally but would not stop being a footballer.

sports.content: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus will host an online watchalong from his Dublin hotel for Saturday’s Nations Championship match against Ireland after the sport’s governing body, World Rugby, suspended him for six matches over comments about referees. Supporters will watch the game on their own televisions while Erasmus appears on camera and reads selected messages. The event is personal, not an official team broadcast, and registration is limited to adults. The suspension followed South Africa’s 21-19 loss to France in Paris. Erasmus questioned why 17 tackles he considered illegal knee-drops had gone unpunished and asked whether officials had manipulated the result. World Rugby’s independent panel ruled that his remarks attacked officials’ credibility and integrity. South Africa Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing. Erasmus will also miss the team’s Nations Championship final match as part of the ban, which covers six matchdays in total.

sports.content: Free-agent left-hander Tarik Skubal has met with the New York Mets, Los Angeles Dodgers and Toronto Blue Jays and is expected to meet with the San Diego Padres as teams pursue the two-time Cy Young Award winner before a possible Major League Baseball lockout. The Mets left their meeting impressed and are viewed as a leading contender, but the Blue Jays and other clubs remain in contention. Skubal is expected to command the richest contract ever given to a pitcher. The current collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, and a lockout would halt transactions. The posting window for Japanese players will not pause and reopen after a lockout, so those seeking to join MLB next season must sign before Dec. 2.

sports.content: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo says he will stop his trademark backflip celebration after Detroit Lions pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL while jumping to celebrate a sack during Sunday’s game in Munich. Skattebo said the injury was difficult to watch and he no longer wants to take the risk. The 24-year-old is returning from a serious ankle injury that required surgery last year. Giants coach John Harbaugh had already urged him to prioritize his health, though the team did not ban the move. Skattebo left open the possibility of bringing it back for a playoff run. He leads the Giants with 496 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 116 carries this season.

sports.title: Mountain biker Hannah Otto sets Kilimanjaro record despite broken leg
sports.summary: Professional mountain biker Hannah Otto became the first known woman to ride up and down Mount Kilimanjaro in one day, completing the ride in 10 hours, 18 minutes on November 3 despite breaking her leg two miles from the finish. She got back on her bike and completed the descent rather than wait for a stretcher; doctor
sports.content: Professional mountain biker Hannah Otto became the first known woman to ride up and down Mount Kilimanjaro in one day, completing the ride in 10 hours, 18 minutes on November 3 despite breaking her leg two miles from the finish. She got back on her bike and completed the descent rather than wait for a stretcher; doctors later diagnosed two tibial plateau fractures and an associated ACL injury. Otto’s ride also supports World Bicycle Relief, which provides bicycles to improve access to education, health care and work. She hopes to raise $165,000 for 1,000 bikes in rural African communities. After surgery in Salt Lake City, she expects to keep weight off her leg for eight to 10 weeks and hopes to return to racing in April 2027.

sports.title: World No. 1 Alexander Zverev contests ex-partner’s lawsuit over trial comments
sports.summary: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev was formally served with a civil lawsuit brought by former partner Brenda Patea on Wednesday, Nov. 18, while competing at the ATP Finals in Turin. Filed in Berlin in September, the suit alleges that Zverev breached their settlement by saying in a June interview that the accusa
sports.content: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev was formally served with a civil lawsuit brought by former partner Brenda Patea on Wednesday, Nov. 18, while competing at the ATP Finals in Turin. Filed in Berlin in September, the suit alleges that Zverev breached their settlement by saying in a June interview that the accusations against him had been disproved and his innocence established. Patea seeks damages and an order barring him from repeating the statements, with a possible fine of up to €250,000 for each violation. The earlier criminal proceedings over Patea’s allegation of bodily harm ended in June 2024 after the pair reached a separate settlement. The court said ending the proceedings did not amount to a verdict on guilt or innocence. Zverev has consistently denied wrongdoing. Zverev’s lawyers say he will defend against the new claim, arguing that his remarks were a protected expression of opinion and did not breach the agreement. Patea’s lawyer says the settlement barred public comment and that Zverev’s statements harmed her reputation and influencer business. Berlin’s regional court confirmed it had received the complaint. No hearing date had been set, and Zverev’s deadline to respond had not yet passed.

sports.title: Bancroft says 2018 Australia team knew of ball-tampering, contradicting Cummins
sports.summary: Former Australia opener Cameron Bancroft has alleged that the entire 2018 touring team and coaching staff knew he was using sandpaper to alter the ball in South Africa, contradicting current Test captain Pat Cummins’ denial. Bancroft also admitted he withheld important details from Cricket Australia’s original investig
sports.content: Former Australia opener Cameron Bancroft has alleged that the entire 2018 touring team and coaching staff knew he was using sandpaper to alter the ball in South Africa, contradicting current Test captain Pat Cummins’ denial. Bancroft also admitted he withheld important details from Cricket Australia’s original investigation to protect teammates, saying he had not given a complete and truthful account. Bancroft says the practice began during the second Test at Port Elizabeth, before he was caught in the third Test at Cape Town. He alleges bowlers discussed whether the ball was swinging enough and that then-coaches Darren Lehmann and David Saker were present when sandpaper was proposed. Those claims remain disputed: Cummins’ representative says the captain’s position has not changed, while former teammate David Warner has backed Bancroft. Cricket Australia says it will consider Bancroft’s account but will not reopen its investigation. Its planned independent forum is voluntary and intended to hear participants’ recollections, not impose further sanctions. The board is finalising the forum’s terms of reference, and Australia’s Test squad announcement for the New Zealand series has been delayed.
